title: How to Stay Safe from UPI and Banking Fraud
summary: Simple habits that stop most fraud, and the exact steps if money leaves your account without your consent.
sectionRefs: Reserve Bank of India - Limited Liability for unauthorised electronic transactions

body.text: Most banking fraud does not need hacking. It only needs you to trust a caller, click a link, or share an OTP. Knowing a few rules keeps your money safe.

items: Never share your OTP, PIN, CVV or password with anyone. No bank or official will ever ask for them.
A request to 'receive money' never needs your PIN. Entering a PIN sends money out.
Do not scan a QR code to receive money.
Do not install screen-sharing or remote-access apps for a 'bank officer'.

body.text: Missed calls and messages that create urgency ('your account will be blocked') are a common trick. Slow down and verify through the official app or branch.
If money leaves your account without consent

items: Inform your bank immediately and ask them to freeze the account and dispute the transaction.
Call the cyber helpline 1930 and report on cybercrime.gov.in.
Give the bank a written complaint and get an acknowledgement.
If it is unresolved, complain to the RBI Ombudsman.

body.text: RBI rules limit your liability for unauthorised electronic transactions, but only if you report quickly. Delay can increase your own loss.
Keep the SMS, email and complaint reference numbers. They are proof of when you reported.

practicalSteps: Never share OTP, PIN, CVV or passwords.
Report a fraudulent transaction to your bank within the shortest possible time.
Escalate to the RBI Ombudsman if the bank does not resolve it within 30 days.
exceptions: If the fraud happened because you shared your credentials or were grossly negligent, your liability may be higher.
Some delays in reporting can shift more liability to you under RBI rules.

faqs.q: Will the bank refund my money?
faqs.a: If you report quickly and were not negligent, RBI rules support limited or zero liability. The bank must resolve your complaint within a set time.
Do not close it before the dispute is settled. Freeze or secure it instead, and keep all records.

misconceptions.myth: If the bank's app shows the transaction, I cannot dispute it.
misconceptions.fact: You can and should dispute any transaction you did not authorise, in writing, to the bank.
